subQuestions.questionText:
PEYPER LIMITED — Financial year ended 28 February 2021

The accountant has incorrectly calculated the closing stock. The weighted-average method should have been used. Calculate the value of the closing stock on 28 February 2021 using the weighted-average method.

Stock of sunglasses:
• 1 March 2020 (opening): 4 000 units at R2 433 000 total value
• 28 February 2021 (closing): 2 400 units — value to be calculated

Purchases during the financial year:
• 31 May 2020: 4 200 units @ R650/unit = R2 730 000
• 15 October 2020: 4 800 units @ R790/unit = R3 792 000
• 11 February 2021: 2 500 units @ R820/unit = R2 050 000
• Total purchases: 11 500 units = R8 572 000
subQuestions.memoText:
Workings:
Total units available = 4 000 + 11 500 = 15 500 units
Total value available = R2 433 000 + R8 572 000 = R11 005 000

Weighted-average cost per unit = R11 005 000 ÷ 15 500 = R710 per unit

Closing stock = 2 400 × R710 = R1 704 000

Mark allocation:
• Numerator R11 005 000 (2 marks)
• Denominator 15 500 units (2 marks)
• Answer R1 704 000 (1 mark — one part correct and × 2 400)

DIGITAL GIANTS LTD — Financial year ends 31 March

Calculate the debt-equity ratio for the financial year ended 31 March 2021.

• Mortgage loan: R2 450 000

= R2 450 000 : R10 387 600
= 0,2 : 1

Note: Must be expressed as x : 1. Shareholders' equity = R7 280 000 + R3 107 600 = R10 387 600 earns 1 mark. One part correct for partial answer.

subQuestions.questionText:
DIGITAL GIANTS LTD — Financial year ends 31 March

Calculate the net asset value (NAV) per share for 31 March 2021.

Information:
• Shareholders' equity on 31 March 2021: R10 387 600
• Shares in issue on 31 March 2020: 700 000
• 120 000 new shares issued on 1 April 2020 at R12,60 per share
• 20 000 shares repurchased on 31 March 2021 (for 50% more than average issue price R9,10)
subQuestions.memoText:
Shares in issue on 31 March 2021 = 700 000 + 120 000 – 20 000 = 800 000 shares (1 mark)

NAV per share = Shareholders' equity × 100 ÷ Number of shares in issue
= R10 387 600 × 100 ÷ 800 000
= 1 298,5 cents

Accept: 1298c / 1299c / R12,98 / R12,99. One part correct for partial answer. R/c not required.

subQuestions.questionText:
DIGITAL GIANTS LTD — Financial year ends 31 March

Calculate the dividend pay-out rate for the financial year ended 31 March 2021.

Information:
• Earnings per share (EPS): 350 cents
• Interim dividend (15 August 2020): 45 cents per share
• Final dividend (31 March 2021): 32 cents per share = R262 400 total
• Net profit after tax: R2 870 000
• Shares in issue on 31 March 2021: 800 000
subQuestions.memoText:
Dividend pay-out rate = (Dividends per share ÷ EPS) × 100
= (45 + 32) ÷ 350 × 100
= 77 ÷ 350 × 100
= 22%

OR
= Total dividends ÷ Net profit after tax × 100
Interim amount = 820 000 × R0,45 = R369 000
Total dividends = R369 000 + R262 400 = R631 400
= R631 400 ÷ R2 870 000 × 100 = 22%

Mark allocation: Numerator 77 cents (2 marks) + Denominator 350 cents (1 mark) + Answer 22% (1 mark — one part correct). Must be shown as a %.

subQuestions.questionText:
DIGITAL GIANTS LTD — Financial year ends 31 March

Calculate the return on average shareholders' equity (ROSHE) for the financial year ended 31 March 2021.

Information:
• Net profit after tax: R2 870 000
• Shareholders' equity on 31 March 2021: R10 387 600
• Shareholders' equity on 31 March 2020: R6 910 000
subQuestions.memoText:
ROSHE = (Net income after tax ÷ Average shareholders' equity) × 100
= R2 870 000 ÷ [½ × (R10 387 600 + R6 910 000)] × 100
= R2 870 000 ÷ R8 648 800 × 100
= 33,2%

Mark allocation:
• Sum R17 297 600 (1 mark)
• Average R8 648 800 (2 marks — half of sum)
• Answer 33,2% (1 mark — one part correct)
Accept 33%. % sign not required.

DIGITAL GIANTS LTD — Cash Flow Statement 2021

Calculate the taxation paid for the 2021 Cash Flow Statement.

Information:
• Income tax per Statement of Comprehensive Income: R1 085 000
• SARS: Income tax on 31 March 2020: R124 000 (Debit — refund due from SARS)
• SARS: Income tax on 31 March 2021: R354 000 (Credit — owing to SARS)
subQuestions.memoText:

= R1 085 000 – R124 000 – R354 000
= R607 000

OR via ledger:

Tax paid = R1 085 000 – R124 000 – R354 000 = R607 000

Mark allocation (1 mark each): R1 085 000, R124 000, R354 000, Final answer R607 000 (one part correct)

subQuestions.questionText:
DIGITAL GIANTS LTD — Cash Flow Statement 2021

Calculate the dividends paid for the 2021 Cash Flow Statement.

Information:
• Shareholders for dividends (31 March 2020): R210 000
• Shareholders for dividends (31 March 2021): R262 400 (= final dividend declared)
• Interim dividend declared 15 August 2020: 45 cents per share
• Final dividend declared 31 March 2021: 32 cents per share = R262 400
• Shares in issue at time of interim: approximately 820 000
subQuestions.memoText:
Dividends paid = Opening Shareholders for dividends + Dividends declared – Closing Shareholders for dividends
= R210 000 + (R369 000 + R262 400) – R262 400
= R210 000 + R369 000
= R579 000

Interim amount = 820 000 shares × R0,45 = R369 000 (2 marks)
The final dividend R262 400 equals the closing balance — it was declared but not yet paid, so it cancels out.

Mark allocation: Opening R210 000 (1 mark) + Interim R369 000 (2 marks) + Answer R579 000 (1 mark — one part correct)

subQuestions.questionText:
DIGITAL GIANTS LTD — Cash Flow Statement 2021

Calculate the proceeds from the sale of fixed assets for the 2021 Cash Flow Statement.

Information:
• Fixed assets at carrying value on 31 March 2021: R8 865 000
• Fixed assets at carrying value on 31 March 2020: R8 878 000
• Total depreciation for the year: R785 000
• Extensions to buildings completed at cost R1 360 000 during the year
• Equipment was sold at carrying value during the year
• No other fixed assets were purchased or sold
subQuestions.memoText:
Using the fixed assets at carrying value account:
Opening CV: R8 878 000
+ Purchases (buildings extension): R1 360 000
– Depreciation: (R785 000)
– Carrying value of assets sold: ?
= Closing CV: R8 865 000

CV sold = R8 878 000 + R1 360 000 – R785 000 – R8 865 000 = R588 000
Since equipment was sold at carrying value: Proceeds = R588 000

Mark allocation (1 mark each): R8 865 000, R8 878 000, R785 000, R1 360 000, Answer R588 000 (one part correct)

subQuestions.questionText:
DIGITAL GIANTS LTD — Cash Flow Statement 2021

Funds used = 20 000 × R13,65 = R273 000

Mark allocation: Correct price/calculation R13,65 (1 mark) + Answer R273 000 (1 mark — one part correct)

subQuestions.questionText:
LIBRA LIMITED — trades in computer hardware and software. CEO: Anton Buys; 5 other directors. Financial years end 30 April.

Financial indicators on 30 April:
• Current ratio: 2021: 0,6:1 | 2020: 1,1:1
• Acid-test ratio: 2021: 0,3:1 | 2020: 0,8:1
• Stockholding period: 2021: 78 days | 2020: 43 days
• Average debtors' collection period: 2021: 58,9 days | 2020: 32,6 days
• Average creditors' payment period: 2021: 75,6 days | 2020: 63,6 days

The current ratio and acid-test ratio show the company's liquidity has deteriorated. Identify TWO other liquidity indicators which also show that the company is likely to have serious liquidity concerns in future. Explain ONE point in EACH case (with figures).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark for indicator + 1 mark for explanation with figures):

1. Stockholding period: Increased from 43 days to 78 days (by 35 days / 81,4%). Cash is tied up in stock; stock is not moving fast enough; danger of obsolescence.

2. Average debtors' collection period: Increased from 32,6 days to 58,9 days (by 26,3 days / 80,1%). Slower collections negatively affect cash flow / poor control over debtors.

Note: Do NOT accept creditors' payment period as a liquidity indicator here.

subQuestions.questionText:
LIBRA LIMITED

The company increased the loan to finance the purchase of additional property in a new suburb, hoping to improve demand for their products.

Financial indicators on 30 April:
• Debt-equity ratio: 2021: 0,7:1 | 2020: 0,2:1
• Return on capital employed (ROTCE): 2021: 6,4% | 2020: 9,1%
• Interest rate on loans: 12%
• Sales: 2021: R8 976 000 | 2020: R11 550 000
• Mark-up % achieved: 2021: 60% | 2020: 75%

(a) Comment on how the increase in the loan affected the risk and gearing in 2021. Quote TWO financial indicators. State ONE point in EACH case (with figures).

(b) Explain whether the decision to purchase additional property had the desired effect on demand (with figures).
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) TWO financial indicators with comment (3 marks each = 6 marks):

POINT 1 — Debt-equity ratio:
Increased from 0,2:1 to 0,7:1 (by 0,5:1). The business is now making much more use of loans, resulting in higher financial risk.

POINT 2 — ROTCE:
Decreased from 9,1% to 6,4% (by 2,7%). The business is negatively geared — the return on capital (6,4%) is lower than the interest rate on loans (12%). The company is not making effective use of borrowed funds.

(b) The decision did NOT have the desired effect (3 marks):
• Sales decreased by R2 574 000 / from R11 550 000 to R8 976 000 / by 22,3%.
• The mark-up reduction from 75% to 60% (lower prices) did not result in more sales.

subQuestions.questionText:
LIBRA LIMITED

A further 80 000 shares were issued at R6,00 per share but the public showed poor interest. Explain why the public was not interested. Quote THREE financial indicators (excluding debt-equity ratio and ROTCE). State ONE point in EACH case (with figures).

Financial indicators on 30 April:
• EPS: 2021: 54 cents | 2020: 102 cents
• DPS: 2021: 25 cents | 2020: 90 cents
• NAV per share: 2021: 732 cents | 2020: 711 cents
• ROSHE: 2021: 4,9% | 2020: 5,3%
• Market price of shares: 2021: 580 cents | 2020: 610 cents
• Interest rate on fixed deposit: 8%
• Mark-up % achieved: 2021: 60% | 2020: 75%
• % operating expenses on sales: 2021: 44,1% | 2020: 32%
subQuestions.memoText:
Any THREE of the following (1 mark indicator + 1 mark figures + 1 mark explanation = 3 marks per point):

1. EPS: Decreased from 102 cents to 54 cents (by 48 cents). Company is struggling to maintain profit levels — poor investment prospect.

2. DPS (Dividends per share): Dropped from 90 cents to 25 cents. Shareholders not receiving a reasonable return.

3. Dividend pay-out rate: Dropped from 88,2% to 46,3%. Directors not focused on returning value to shareholders.

4. ROSHE: Dropped from 5,3% to 4,9%; still below fixed deposit interest rate (8%). Investing in shares gives a lower return than a bank deposit.

5. Market price / NAV: At R6,00, shares were expensive relative to the market price of R6,10 (2020) or R5,80 (2021); directors then sold at R4,80 — shows lack of investor confidence.

6. NAV (711 cents 2020) higher than market price (610 cents) — indicates low demand for shares even before the new issue.

7. Liquidity: Current ratio 0,6:1 and acid-test 0,3:1 — the company may struggle to meet short-term obligations.

subQuestions.questionText:
LIBRA LIMITED

At the AGM, shareholders complained that the Remunerations Committee was negligent and that CEO Anton Buys did not deserve his fees.

Directors' fees on 30 April:
• Director's fees paid to CEO (Anton Buys): 2021: R2 900 000 | 2020: R2 000 000
• Total fees paid to 5 other directors: 2021: R3 000 000 | 2020: R3 000 000

Other indicators: EPS 2021: 54c (2020: 102c); ROSHE: 4,9% (5,3%); ROTCE: 6,4% (9,1%); % operating expenses on sales: 44,1% (32%)

State TWO different points to justify the shareholders' opinion. Quote figures or financial indicators.
subQuestions.memoText:
TWO valid points (2 marks each: 1 for point + 1 for figure):

POINT 1 (Compulsory — must comment on CEO's fees):
• Anton Buys gave himself a 45% increase (from R2 000 000 to R2 900 000 = +R900 000).
• The CEO's R900 000 increase is 30% of what the 5 other directors collectively earn.
• Other directors received no increase (still R3 000 000 total / R600 000 each).

POINT 2 (any ONE of):
• EPS dropped from 102 cents to 54 cents (by 48 cents) — poor performance under his leadership.
• ROSHE dropped from 5,3% to 4,9%.
• ROTCE dropped from 9,1% to 6,4%.
• Operating expenses increased from 32% to 44,1% of sales — poor expense control.

subQuestions.questionText:
LIBRA LIMITED — Share capital and shareholding:
• Shares in issue: 2021: 2 450 000 | 2020: 2 400 000
• Shares owned by Anton Buys: 2021: 1 240 000 | 2020: 1 270 000
• On 1 May 2020, 30 000 shares repurchased from Anton Buys at R12,00 per share (none of the other 5 directors supported this decision)
• 80 000 new shares issued on 30 June 2020 at R4,80 (originally listed at R6,00)
• NAV per share (2020): 711 cents | Market price (2020): 610 cents

(a) Explain why the other directors were unhappy with the price paid for the shares repurchased from Anton Buys. State TWO points. Quote financial indicators or figures to support EACH point.

(b) Give a calculation to show whether the repurchase of these shares affected Anton Buys' status as majority shareholder, or not.
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) TWO points (2 marks each = 4 marks; both points may be in the same statement; 2020 figures must be quoted):

POINT 1: The shares were repurchased at R12,00 — R4,89 above the NAV per share of 711 cents. The business paid an inflated/unreasonable price (169% of NAV), compromising its cash flow.

POINT 2: The repurchase price of R12,00 is R5,90 more than the market price of R6,10 (610 cents in 2020). There is no demand for shares at that level — the price is unreasonable.

(b) Calculation (3 marks):
Anton Buys' percentage = 1 240 000 ÷ 2 450 000 × 100 = 50,6%
OR = 1 240 000 ÷ 2 370 000 × 100 = 52,3% (using shares before July 2020 issue)

Conclusion: Anton Buys still holds more than 50% — he remains the majority shareholder. The repurchase did NOT affect his majority status.

Mark allocation: Numerator 1 240 000 (1 mark) + Denominator 2 450 000 or 2 370 000 (1 mark) + Result as % (1 mark — one part correct)

LIBRA LIMITED

Excellence Limited (renowned for good corporate governance) has offered to purchase the remaining 2 550 000 unissued shares at a price considerably more than current market value. Anton Buys says he will vote against this proposal. The other directors strongly favour accepting the offer.

(a) Explain what is meant by good corporate governance and explain why it is important to shareholders.

(b) Explain a possible reason why Anton Buys says he will vote against the proposal by Excellence Ltd.

(c) The other directors feel Anton Buys is abusing his position as CEO and majority shareholder.
   • Explain why you agree with them.
   • Give the directors advice on how they should handle this.
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Good corporate governance (3 marks):
Explanation (2 marks — any valid point):
• Managing the business on sound business and ethical principles.
• Looking after the interests of all stakeholders (including the community) by being fair, equitable, and transparent.
• Ensuring proper rules, policies and practices are in place to create long-term shareholder value.

Importance to shareholders (1 mark):
• Positively impacts the image/goodwill of the business.
• Leads to improvement in share price.
• Attracts potential investors.
• Builds confidence in management.

(b) Reason Anton Buys will vote against (2 marks — any valid point):
• He will lose his majority control on the Board if Excellence Ltd acquires all unissued shares.
• He may lose his CEO status and power.
• He may be investigated for negligence/misconduct.
• He will not be able to manipulate his own remuneration in future.

(c) Why you agree with directors (2 marks):
• He has taken irresponsible decisions that serve his own interests (e.g., 45% salary increase while company performance deteriorated; voted for his own inflated share repurchase against all others' wishes).

Advice to directors (2 marks — any valid point):
• Call a special meeting of shareholders.
• Issue a grievance report.
• Start disciplinary/investigation proceedings for mismanagement.
• Ask Anton Buys to step aside as CEO.
